startup.name: Blaxel
startup.description: Cloud infrastructure for AI agents: sandboxes that scale to zero and resume in about 25 ms with memory state kept, plus a shared filesystem and networking primitives. Developers pay usage based fees. Team of 12 in San Francisco, with a live product. Forecast as of 2025-04-07, window to 2026-11-17 (about 19 months).

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is in the Spring 2025 batch, so this is shown for completeness. Start from the roughly 1 percent prior for a random applicant (0.6 to 2 percent range). Adjust up for a twelve person team with a working product, an infrastructure wedge that fits YC's AI agent interest and technical credibility, then hold near 2 percent because no revenue is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly say no because agent sandboxes are a crowded, capital heavy category: E2B, Modal and Daytona already ship similar primitives, and hyperscalers can add microVM sandboxes. Without named paying customers or usage growth, the partners may see a performance claim of 25 ms resume rather than a reason developers switch.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag "Developer Tools" gave seed 46% / 51% / 57% (n=219, cond 51%); --industry B2B gave 47% / 53% / 59%. Time rule: 2022+ months to seed p50 6, p75 14.2 in time_to_milestones.csv, so about 85 percent of ever reachers have raised by 19 months.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever anchor 0.51 to 0.57 for an infrastructure company with a team of 12 and a live product, scaled by about 0.88 for the 19 month window, gives about 0.47 to 0.50. Held at 0.50, within 1.25 times the anchor, with no lift for the AI agent theme; the odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: A small post YC round of about $1M to $3M from angels and a micro fund, the most common outcome when a team has early pilots but no repeatable sales motion. It is the largest band because the 2022 and later seed table (p25 $2.0M, median $3.5M) mixes in YC deal sized checks.
A conventional institutional seed of $3M to $6M led by a seed fund, matching the 2022 and later table median of $3.5M and the p75 of $5.2M for the cohort.

A $6M to $12M seed, which happens when a lead fund prices on market heat. Among confirmed 2026 raises above $1M the median was $6.0M, but press covers large rounds more, so this band is kept at a minority.
An upside seed above $12M, reached only if the company shows unusual early revenue or a top fund competes for it; rare in the YC data and kept small.

ladder.why_it_fails: Window is 19 months (2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17); seed means an outside round above about $1M. The most likely miss is that usage stays hobbyist and revenue small while E2B, Modal and Daytona collect the early agent developers and hyperscalers add microVM sandboxes. Beam and Cerebrium raised seeds of $3.5M and $8.5M in 2022, but Mystic and Cakework, two person serverless teams, ended without a clear institutional round.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag "Developer Tools" gave series_a 12% / 13% / 23% with cond 26% (n=100); B2B cond 26% (n=468). Time rule: 2022+ months to series A p25 19.4, p50 28.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Ever conditional of 0.26 scaled by about 0.45 for a 19 month window that ends before the median A timing of 28 months, rounded up to 0.12 for a hot infrastructure theme. More than 2x below the anchor because most A rounds close later than the window.

bands.rationale: A thin or bridge style Series A of $6M to $10M, common when growth is real but revenue is still small; below the 2022 and later p25 of $11M, so it stands for the soft band.
The central Series A of $10M to $18M, bracketing the 2022 and later median of $15M and p25 to p75 of $11M to $21M.
A larger A of $18M to $30M that top funds lead when growth looks category defining; current market data shows A deal sizes near $17M to $20M.
An upside A above $30M, seen only for a few AI companies with very fast revenue; rare and kept at a small share.

ladder.why_it_fails: An A inside 19 months needs usage based revenue that compounds, and infrastructure rounds of $10M plus go to companies with clear lead position. Sandbox vendors compete on price and cold start time, which can be matched, and the A cohort of Beam and Cerebrium took more than two years. If hyperscaler primitives close the performance gap, Blaxel is left with a thin margin product and no lead investor.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag "Developer Tools" gave series_b cond 19% (n=26); B2B cond 21% (n=123). Long run, not window numbers.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Equal to the cohort anchor; this step is the long run chance beyond the forecast window and I do not lift it for the AI infrastructure theme.

bands.rationale: A smaller or flat Series B of $15M to $30M, typical when the A cohort slows; includes down or extension rounds.
The central Series B of $30M to $50M, matching the 2022 and later median of $40M with p25 to p75 of $27M to $55M.
A growth B of $50M to $80M for companies with clear scaled revenue.
An upside B above $80M for category leaders, rare among YC companies.

ladder.why_it_fails: A Series B requires infrastructure spend at real scale, either many enterprise accounts or a few very large agent platforms. Usage based revenue is volatile when a customer switches providers, and cloud vendors set the price floor. Beam, Cerebrium and Replicate show that few serverless AI platforms reach a B; most stop at a seed or A or are absorbed.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --years 2022-2024 --tag "Developer Tools" gave series_c cond 0% (n=5); B2B cond 19% (n=26); older eras 36 to 43 percent.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Within 1.25 times the B2B anchor; developer tools cohort has too few cases and older eras ran higher.

bands.rationale: A modest later round of $30M to $60M, including down rounds and structured deals.
The central round of $60M to $120M, bracketing the 2022 and later series C median of $74M.
A large growth round of $120M to $250M for a clear leader.
A mega round above $250M, which only a handful of YC companies have reached.

ladder.why_it_fails: A growth round past B needs a defensible position as the default agent runtime, which collides with AWS, Google Cloud and Cloudflare. Replicate reached a Series B and was then acquired, a more common end than an independent growth round, because compute platforms need capital to grow and the cloud vendors can bundle.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The likely failure is a feature level win that turns into a commodity: agent sandboxes become a hyperscaler primitive and margins compress, leaving a lean team acqui-hired or stalled at seed. Developer tools cohorts show 14 to 17 percent shut down and 13 to 17 percent acquired. A $1B outcome needs the platform to be the default agent runtime, which only a few infrastructure companies achieve.

analogs.relevance: Serverless GPU compute for AI developers (W22)
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $3.5M seed in May 2022 led by Tiger Global, then repositioned toward open source serverless compute for agents; shows seed access for this infrastructure shape but a slow path past it.
Reached reported millions in ARR through partnerships and raised an $8.5M seed, a good outcome that came about a year after the batch.

analogs.relevance: Low latency API to run and deploy ML models (W21)
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised roughly $3M to $3.8M of seed money per aggregators but is now inactive, a seed then stall failure.

analogs.relevance: Serverless hosting API for developer platforms (W23)
analogs.outcome_summary: Two former AWS engineers; inactive with no round beyond YC found, a failure when a platform vendor and cheaper compute crowded the space.

analogs.relevance: Run ML models in the cloud (W20)
analogs.outcome_summary: Quiet for years, then a $12.5M Series A in 2023 and a Series B, later acquired; shows infrastructure can win but takes timing.

killers.risk: Hyperscalers and funded sandbox vendors compete on price and features
killers.evidence: E2B, Modal and Daytona already sell code sandboxes for agents, and AWS Lambda and Cloudflare offer isolated execution that could add stateful features.
killers.mitigation: Win a specific workload such as high concurrency standby sandboxes with measurable cost savings and sign annual commits.

killers.risk: Usage stays developer experiments, not paid production workloads
killers.evidence: Agent builders are mostly early stage and spend little; Beam repositioned after serverless GPU demand did not convert as expected.
killers.mitigation: Target five agent companies with real production traffic and price on committed usage.

killers.risk: The 25 ms resume and scale to zero claims are copied once microVM snapshot technology is open source
killers.evidence: Firecracker based snapshots are open source and other vendors already advertise fast boot, so the technical edge is not exclusive.
killers.mitigation: Pair the runtime with sticky primitives such as shared filesystem and networking that raise switching costs.

competition_now.name: E2B
competition_now.what: Open source sandboxes for AI agent code execution built on Firecracker
competition_now.traction: Known developer adoption among AI agent builders as of early 2025

competition_now.name: Modal
competition_now.what: Serverless compute platform that offers sandboxes and GPU jobs
competition_now.traction: Well funded infrastructure company with large developer base

competition_now.name: Daytona
competition_now.what: Dev environment and sandbox infrastructure for AI coding agents
competition_now.traction: Open source project with growing developer interest

competition_now.name: AWS Lambda
competition_now.what: Hyperscaler serverless execution that could add stateful isolated environments

technical_complexity.rationale: Fast snapshot resume with preserved memory, isolation and multi tenant scheduling are hard systems engineering that a team of 12 with infrastructure experience can build, and when working this is a real moat. The risk is that hyperscaler primitives or open source Firecracker tooling close the gap, and uptime and security expectations are high.

takeover_risk.rationale: Cloud vendors and funded rivals can ship stateful sandbox features within a year and own distribution through existing cloud accounts. The incentive is strong because agent workloads drive compute spend, so takeover risk is high.

evidence.claim: Multiple vendors and open source projects compete to sell code execution sandboxes to agent builders, which shows developer demand for isolated runtime (vendor material, directional).
AI giants and developers pay for sandboxed execution of generated code; microVM isolation is described as the minimum for untrusted agent code in vendor comparisons.

roadmap.goal: Show real agent workloads running on the platform
actions: Get 5 agent companies to run production traffic
Publish cold start and cost benchmarks against E2B and Modal
roadmap.proof: 5 production customers and public benchmark data

actions: Move customers to monthly minimum commits
Add enterprise features such as VPC and audit logs
roadmap.proof: $30K to $50K monthly recurring revenue with 3 or more customers above $5K a month

roadmap.goal: Become the default runtime for a segment of agent builders
actions: Reach 10x growth in sandbox hours with stable gross margin
Ship the shared filesystem and networking primitives as sticky products
roadmap.proof: $1M to $2M ARR and gross margin above 50 percent

pros.point: Strong technical wedge with measurable claims
pros.evidence: Scale to zero after 1 second and resume in under 25 ms with memory state preserved is a concrete, testable performance claim.

pros.point: Larger team than most batch companies
pros.evidence: Twelve people at the start of the batch gives capacity to build an infrastructure product and support early customers.

brand.name: Blaxel
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Blaxel" --era 2022+ gave kind invented_or_proper, 6 characters, 2 syllables, no suffix or digits.
strengths: Short, distinctive, easy to type as a domain and CLI name
Invented word with no category baggage
weaknesses: Does not signal agents or infrastructure
Spelling is not obvious from hearing it
brand.rationale: An invented short name is common among YC infrastructure companies such as Modal or Replicate, and for developer tools the brand mostly comes from docs and product quality, so the effect is neutral and does not move the ladder.

narrative.headline: A technically credible agent infrastructure company in a crowded, capital hungry category; a seed is about even within 19 months.
narrative.general_summary: Blaxel sells sandboxes and storage primitives for autonomous AI agents with a team of 12 and a live product. Agent infrastructure drew heavy investor attention in 2025 and the YC data shows serverless AI platforms such as Beam and Cerebrium raising seeds within a year, but also Mystic and Cakework ending without a clear next round. In a 19 month window the anchor puts a seed above $1M near 50 percent and a Series A inside the window near 12 percent given seed. Hyperscalers and E2B, Modal and Daytona are the main threats. Odds here do not rank this company against others.

assumptions: Forecast made blind from the input file only; the window runs 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17, about 19 months.
Seed means an outside round above about $1M; the YC deal alone does not count.
Seed and Series A odds are for the window; Series B and C odds are long run conditional rates.
Seed bands use the AI native shape (20/35/30/15) because the team has 12 people and a live product, per the winners test rule.
Web search results from the company's own blog and results dated after the as_of date were ignored (LEAK-WEB: blaxel); only third party market pages were used for need and competition.
